channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Election 2026 live updates: Americans cast their votes
item.description: There are key House and Senate races that could determine control of Congress.

item.title: France's dermatology crisis: Patients desperate for appointments
item.description: Around 200,000 cases of skin cancer are diagnosed in France every year. Yet as more and more patients seek medical advice, getting an appointment with a dermatologist is becoming increasingly difficult. Half the country's dermatologists are nearing retirement, and only around 100 new specialists are trained up each year. Faced with this growing shortage, some are coming up with innovative solutions. FRANCE 24's Aurore Dupuis and Sonia Baritello report.

item.title: Family wealth, Epstein, ‘vanity projects’: How Democrats plan to investigate Trump after midterms
item.description: Democrats are preparing to launch a flurry of investigations into President Donald Trump’s administration and business dealings if they retake one or both chambers of Congress, devising strategies to circumvent obstruction from the White House and avoid the impeachment deadlock that consumed the US legislature during Trump’s first term in office.

item.title: Russian households face increasing financial strain as war in Ukraine drags on
item.description: As Moscow continues to launch strikes across Ukraine, Russian citizens are facing increasing financial strain. Since the start of the war in 2022, utility bills in Russia have risen by more than 50% – over 13% this year alone. These rising costs come as the country grapples with ongoing drone attacks originating from Ukraine.

item.title: Ukraine and Russia are taking the war underground as drones saturate the battlefield
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky last week heralded the success of Operation Veles, during which Kyiv sent troops deep into a disused gas pipeline in the Kupiansk region to confront Russian troops. These underground tactics, which Russian forces have been using for more than two years to slip past Ukrainian lines, are giving Kyiv a new strategy on the battlefield.

item.title: US Midterms: Texas Democrat Talarico holds last rally ahead of vote
item.description: Texas Democratic nominee James Talarico held a final rally Monday ahead of US midterm elections on November 3. His race against Republican Ken Paxton could determine which party holds a majority in the Senate. If Talarico wins, it will be the first time a Texas Senate seat's turned blue since 1988.

item.title: US midterm elections: Over 58 million Americans cast early ballots
item.description: How powerful is US President Donald Trump? That’s the question pollsters have been asking in the lead-up to the midterm elections. Polls have opened in dozens of US states in what is widely considered a referendum on Donald Trump. Most polls suggest Democrats will take back the House of Representatives, but could they also take the Senate and stymie Trump’s agenda during his final two years in office?

item.title: US midterms: Talarico seeks to break Democrats' 30-year losing streak in Texas
item.description: In Texas, Democratic candidate James Talarico is leading the polls ahead of a high-stakes US Senate race against Republican Ken Paxton. The contest is one of the most closely watched battles of the midterm elections, with Democrats hoping to end a 30-year losing streak in the state. FRANCE 24's Andrés Espinal reports from Austin, Texas.

item.title: Brazil keeps a close eye on US midterm elections
item.description: Brazil is keeping a close eye on the US midterm elections. Since Donald Trump's return to the White House, relations between Brasilia and Washington have grown increasingly tense. On the economic front, aggressive trade policies have subjected Brazilian imports to some of the steepest tariffs globally, exacerbating friction with the Trump administration. FRANCE 24's correspondent in Rio de Janeiro Jan Onoszko has more.

item.title: ‘Vile terrorist attack’: Russia bombs Ukraine aid centre
item.description: A Russian “double tap” strike on a Ukrainian school being used as an aid distribution has killed at least 31 people, according to local authorities, with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky dubbing it a “vile terrorist attack”.

item.title: Trump focused on 'what's important to him': 'Tone-deaf for a normally shrewd populist operator'
item.description: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Doug Heye, Republican strategist, founder of Douglas Media, and former Communications Director for the Republican National Committee (RNC). As Americans head to the polls, Republicans face a challenge that goes beyond the familiar electoral backlash against an incumbent president. For Heye, Donald Trump's greatest political vulnerability may lie in the widening gap between his rhetoric of economic success and voters' everyday financial anxieties. "For a lot of voters, they see him focused on what's important to him, not what's important to them," Heye explains. Yet he also cautions against interpreting Democratic gains as a sign of renewed confidence in the opposition. Rather than a resurgence of partisan enthusiasm, the elections may expose an electorate increasingly disillusioned with both parties.

item.title: Trump cuts Israeli military aid: $3.8 billion in security assistance slashed
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Tuesday, November 3, said he made a deal with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for Washington to stop providing $3.8 billion in funding to Israel after the end of this year. FRANCE 24's Jerusalem correspondent, Noga Tarnopolsky, has more.

item.title: WATCH: On the ground in Maine on Election Day
item.description: ABC News’ Will Reeve reports from Maine, where Democrats are trying to unseat longtime incumbent Republican Sen. Susan Collins.

item.title: Trump says US will end military aid to Israel by end of year
item.description: Trump said he and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu "made a deal months ago."

item.title: For Ukraine's Kherson region, a short ceasefire meant a momentary return to normal life
item.description: In Kherson city, usually seething with Russian drones, friends met at cafes, families were out together and shoppers stocked up. "The city seems alive," said one resident, "just like it used to be."

item.title: US midterms: Michigan Senate candidate El-Sayed becomes Democrats' rising star
item.description: In the US midterm elections, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers are testing two sharply different strategies to win over voters in one of the nation's premier swing states on Tuesday, November 3, in a closely watched race that could determine control of the Senate. Progressive candidate El-Sayed has so far outpolled his Republican rival and is emerging as one of the Democratic Party's rising stars.

item.title: US midterms: Michigan candidate El-Sayed pledges to tackle the affordability crisis
item.description: The cost of living is one of the main concerns for many US voters as the midterm elections get underway. In Michigan, Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed has pledged to "take the money out of politics and put it in your pocket", as FRANCE 24 correspondent Jessica Le Masurier reports.

item.title: A cultural stroll through Paris with actors François-Xavier Demaison and François Morel
item.description: This week, we bring you a special programme dedicated to theatre. Valérie Fayolle takes us to the Renaissance Theatre, where François-Xavier Demaison takes us behind the scenes of "Laponie". The fiesty comedy shows how a family's holiday gathering can quickly turn into a settling of scores. "Theatre is one of our last collective experiences. It's magnificent, we're in a bubble," he tells us.

item.title: King Charles says he has greater understanding of 'horrors' of slavery, falls short of apology
item.description: King Charles III told the heads of 56 Commonwealth countries on Tuesday that he has a greater understanding of the horrors of slavery, calling it a "shameful chapter of history". This comes as Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he was open to the United Kingdom apologising for the transatlantic slave trade.

item.title: 'Your donut, your vote': Texas group uses free food to attract young voters
item.description: US voters on Tuesday headed to the polls in midterm elections that could shape the political future of the country. But navigating the voting process can sometimes discourage voters – particularly younger ones. In Texas, an organisation reached out to them directly by handing out free food, to then help them overcome these obstacles. FRANCE 24's Special envoy Tarek Kai reports from Austin.

item.title: Spanish police investigating after soccer player dies following on-field collision
item.description: Spanish police have opened an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter after a soccer player died following an on-field collision with the opposing team’s goalkeeper in a second-division match

item.title: Political parallels in France and the US: Anger at the ballot box and in the streets
item.description: Anger has long been a driving force for political change, but with the midterm elections in the US and the ongoing protests in France, widespread anger in both nations is currently front and centre. We take a look at some of the common issues causing this anger on both sides of the Atlantic, including the rising cost of living, a loss of faith in institutions and an eroding of the social contract.

item.title: US midterms: All eyes on crucial Michigan Senate race
item.description: In the US midterm elections, the Senate race in Michigan has been one of the most closely watched in the country. It took an unexpected turn on Sunday after Democratic Congresswoman Haley Stevens endorsed Republican Mike Rogers over Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed. Both candidates made their final pitches to voters during campaign rallies on Monday evening, November 2. FRANCE 24's Jessica Le Masurier reports.

item.title: MPs urge online retailers to stop selling AI toys over child harm fears
item.description: AI toys with built-in chatbots could expose children to psychological harms and inappropriate material, according to MPs and peers who are urging Amazon and eBay to stop selling them.

item.title: High-stakes midterms are test for future of Congress and Trump's presidency
item.description: Here’s a look at some key Senate, House and gubernatorial races to watch that could help define the outcome of the 2026 midterm elections.

item.title: Reform councillor charged with 35 offences including rape
item.description: A Reform UK councillor has been charged with 35 offences, including 12 counts of rape, the Crown Prosecution Service said.

item.title: Trump says US will halt $4 billion in aid to Israel after end of the year
item.description: President Donald Trump on Tuesday said that the United States will stop $4 billion in funding to Israel after the end of this year. While speaking to Fox News' Fox and Friends, the US president added that Israel no longer needed the aid from Washington, and that some politicians were using the funding to criticise Republicans.

item.title: 2026 Prix Goncourt: France's prestigious literary prize awarded to Philippe Jaenada
item.description: France’s prestigious literary prize “The Goncourt” was awarded on Monday to writer Philippe Jaenada. The prize carries a symbolic reward of only 10 euros, but results in considerable recognition and book sales for the winning author. FRANCE 24’s Culture reporter Olivia Salazar-Winspear reports from the Parisian restaurant where the jury made the call.

item.title: Americans vote in key midterms set to upend Trump presidency
item.description: Americans voted on Tuesday in pivotal midterm elections with Democrats hoping to seize control of Congress and impose the first significant checks on Donald Trump's chaotic second term in the White House. Republicans losing the House would give Democrats the power to stall Trump's legislative agenda and launch sweeping investigations of his administration. FRANCE 24's Fraser Jackson reports from Washington, DC.

item.title: Israeli opposition leaders vow to remove Netanyahu quickly but path unclear
item.description: The Israeli opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot pledged Tuesday to form a government quickly to oust Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu but remained unclear on how, with divisions over whether to ally with Arab lawmakers. Arab-majority parties last week won 19 seats in the 120-member parliament. Eisenkot's diverse opposition bloc won 48 seats while Netanyahu's camp secured 53, of which 27 are from his Likud party.

item.title: Indian navy rescues 20 crew from Iranian fishing boat hijacked off Somalia
item.description: he operation involved a warship, a maritime surveillance aircraft and marine commandos. The hijacking followed a resurgence of Somali piracy across the Gulf of Aden and western Indian Ocean.

item.title: Famous man loses injunction bid against two news organisations over allegations - but can't be named yet
item.description: A man has lost his bid for an injunction against two media outlets to prevent the publication of allegations against him, a judge has ruled.

item.title: WATCH: New states in play as record gas prices hit on Election Day
item.description: ABC News’ Chief Washington Correspondent Jon Karl and Chief Business Correspondent Rebecca Jarvis break down why states in deep-red territory are in play and the state of the economy on Election Day.

item.title: WATCH: State of the race: Paths to victory
item.description: ABC News’ Senior Political Correspondent Rachel Scott has the latest on the state of the races as voters head to the polls across the country.

item.title: US midterm elections: A referendum on President Donald Trump?
item.description: Americans deliver their verdict on Donald Trump's tumultuous first term in midterm elections that threaten to shatter his grip on Washington, with Democrats poised to seize the House and within striking distance of the Senate.

item.title: Californians vote on ballot initiative to impose one-time tax on billionaires
item.description: This Tuesday, Californians are voting on a landmark plan to impose a one-time tax on billionaires to fund the state's healthcare system. We take a closer look. Also on the show: global oil prices fell sharply on the eve of the US midterm elections. This came after Iran said it was holding intensive talks through mediators towards negotiating peace and signalled that it was ready to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if the US accepted its conditions. Both Brent and WTI fell by around 8 percent.

item.title: Australia's social media ban challenged by Reddit and rights group in court
item.description: Australia's landmark social media ban for under-16s faces challenges in court over accusations that it amounts to censorship and creates privacy issues.

item.title: Train knifeman appeared to believe 17-year-old victim was the devil, court hears
item.description: A man who stabbed a teenager on a train in London appeared to believe the boy was the devil, a court has heard.

item.title: Bomb threats reported on multiple flights, including two from UK airports
item.description: At least seven flights, including two from the UK, have been affected by bomb threats, which caused unplanned landings and temporary airport closures.

item.title: WATCH: David Muir shares New Jersey students' determination in 100-Yard Food Drive Challenge
item.description: Students at Howell High School filled their football field with over a quarter million pounds of food for the nonprofit, Dermer Dreams. David Muir reports on the volunteers that delivered.

item.title: WATCH: Lucky fisherman catches fish worth $1M
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a mechanic in Australia whose life just changed by a fishing contest.

item.title: WATCH: Man complete 31,000-mile walk around the world after 28 years
item.description: A British adventurer who has been walking around the world for almost three decades returned to his childhood home Monday.

item.title: These key Senate races will determine which party controls the body next year
item.description: As both parties prepare for the final leg of the campaign, here are some of the most closely watched Senate races.

item.title: Death toll hits 29 after Russian strike on Ukrainian aid site, with 48 still missing
item.description: Russia launched 289 attack drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles across nine regions, President Zelenskyy said in an online post that noted the barrage coincided with U.S. elections.

item.title: Four types of House races to watch on election night to know how it might go
item.description: As polls close on Election Day and results start rolling in, these are some of the House races that will help explain how the midterms are unfolding.

item.title: Boy, 14, arrested after reports of Bradley Lowery taunt at football match
item.description: A 14-year-old boy has been arrested after reports that a Coventry fan appeared to taunt Sunderland supporters about Bradley Lowery.

item.title: Spanish footballer dies after on-field collision
item.description: Tenerife football player Jesus de Miguel has died after suffering a cardiac arrest following an on-field collision in a match on Monday.

item.title: New restrictions at Texas Tech are changing what professors can teach
item.description: The rules have led to changes in course materials, prompted accusations of censorship and fueled pushback from faculty and students, including faculty departures, student protests and a federal lawsuit.

item.title: How NPR makes race calls in the 2026 election
item.description: Race calls are a critical part of election night and NPR partners with the Associated Press to make those calls. Here's how we do it.

item.title: From 'model minority' to target, anti-Indian hate on the rise
item.description: A massacre allegedly targeting Hindu Americans was recently thwarted, but researchers say it helps to illustrate a growing and increasingly mainstream hate directed at South Asians in the U.S.

item.title: 'Messy,' 'divided' and 'scary': swing voters rate the country ahead of Election Day
item.description: One last check in with the Swing Shift voters before Election Day. All of them voted for President Trump. Now, they're rating his presidency and deciding who to support when he's not on the ballot.

item.title: WATCH: 5 people at Chili's in North Carolina suffer burns after margarita mix-up
item.description: Three customers and two employees at a Chili's restaurant suffered chemical burns after an employee mistakenly used a cleaning powder instead of sugar to make the drinks, health officials say.

item.title: Cyber attacks affect UK meat processing industry, top security official says
item.description: Cyber attacks have affected the UK meat processing industry, a top security official has said in the wake of hacks that hit supermarkets across Europe.

item.title: US carries out 'limited strikes' on Qeshm Island in Iran
item.description: The US military has carried out "limited strikes" on Qeshm Island in Iran - hours before the midterms are due to take place.

item.title: British troops will be allowed to fire at Russian forces if attacked during multinational mission
item.description: British troops will be allowed to fire back at Russian forces if attacked as part of a multinational mission to secure any future peace in Ukraine, Western officials have said.

item.title: Judge blasts DOJ in dismissing case against ex-FBI agents who probed Hunter Biden
item.description: A judge has dismissed the DOJ's federal false statements case against two former FBI agents accused of lying to Congress about past investigations of Hunter Biden.

item.title: GOP touts Stevens endorsement while El-Sayed's campaign reports a record haul
item.description: As Republicans touted Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens' 11th-hour endorsement of GOP Michigan U.S. Senate candidate Mike Rogers, Democrats downplayed its impact.

item.title: How do midterm candidates plan to fight inflation? Economists evaluate proposals
item.description: Proposals include tax cuts and an end to the Iran war.

item.title: What you need to know about the Election Day Voter Poll
item.description: The Election Day Voter Poll helps answer the question of who won and why and explain what issues were important in the election.

item.title: WATCH: Seahawks inspire young leaders beyond the field
item.description: ABC News' Kayna Whitworth reports live from Lumen Field in Seattle on how the Seahawks are helping kids build leadership skills and pursue their dreams.

item.title: WATCH: Video of ICE agent apparently pointing gun in bystander's face during arrest
item.description: ICE is facing new scrutiny over a video that allegedly shows an ICE agent pointing a gun in the face of a bystander in California.

item.title: FIFA to share documents relating to World Cup sell-off plan
item.description: FIFA will give members of its ruling council access to some documents for the first time related to the World Cup sell-off, Sky News understands.

item.title: WATCH: A look at the state of the midterm races
item.description: ABC News' Senior Political Correspondent Rachel Scott breaks down the state of play as a new New York Times/Siena poll shows Democrats are gaining ground, slightly pulling ahead in key Senate races.

item.title: WATCH: Sisters go from lifesaving surgery to running a marathon
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to cancer survivor Kate Stevens, who received a bone marrow transplant from her sister and, around two decades later, ran a marathon with her.

item.title: 'Everything is destroyed': Hackers target refrigerators in new cyber attacks
item.description: Cyber hackers have targeted fridges and freezers in supermarkets in several European countries including Ireland – causing temperatures to increase and food to spoil.

item.title: Advocates rally voters after dozens of polling sites closed in 'swing' Texas county
item.description: Community and advocacy groups in Tarrant County, Texas, are rallying to get voters to the polls after officials shut down dozens of polling locations before the midterms.

item.title: WATCH: Thrilling finishes at NYC marathon
item.description: Sweden's Andreas Almgren won his first men's NYC marathon, and Kenya's Shelia Chepkirui won her second NYC marathon.

item.title: British backpackers in Australia could face changes to visa rules
item.description: British backpackers in Australia could be forced to spend more time in regional areas under proposed changes to the country's working holiday visa.

item.title: WATCH: The volunteers helping get the NYC marathon running
item.description: While the spotlight will be on the nearly 60,000 people running the course, they would not be there without the help of thousands of volunteers on the sidelines.

item.title: Election workers describe toll of DOJ threats in court filings
item.description: California election officials described the Trump administration’s legal threats as having consequences on their mental health, according to court papers.

item.title: States push back on Trump's noncitizen voting claims
item.description: The Trump administration has warned several states that their voter rolls include noncitizens, but many of those claims haven't held up to scrutiny.
